title: A general platform for targeted, adaptable phage treatment

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reusable system for turning bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—into reliably targeted treatments for diverse bacterial infections. It would connect identification of the infecting bacterial isolate with selection or adaptation of suitable phages, reproducible production, delivery to the infection site and assessment of patient benefit. Its generality would lie in repeatedly applying this process to new isolates, rather than relying on a single phage preparation to treat every infection. This is a conceptual synthesis of the proposed capability, not a claim that such a platform has been achieved.

The central scientific task is to connect phage host specificity and bacterial susceptibility with effective treatment in patients. A phage that kills a patient's isolate in a laboratory assay is a candidate treatment; that observation alone does not establish that it reaches the infection, remains active there or improves clinical outcomes. The proposed platform therefore includes diagnosis, treatment matching, manufacturing and clinical evaluation as essential parts of the capability.

significance.text: As a conditional consequence of the proposed breakthrough, reliable treatment across diverse isolates and infections would create a reusable antimicrobial capability. Instead of developing each treatment as an isolated intervention, clinicians could draw on a repeatable process for identifying or producing an effective, narrowly targeted preparation. Adaptability could be particularly valuable when the infecting isolate resists available antibiotics, although antibiotic resistance would not itself establish susceptibility to a particular phage.

A further conditional possibility is that narrow targeting could help preserve non-target microbes while treating the pathogen. That benefit would need to be measured rather than inferred from targeting alone. The platform could also support responses to changing bacterial populations, but neither adaptability nor initial treatment success would guarantee durable resistance control, prevention of recurrence or universal coverage. Diagnosis, manufacturing controls, clinical testing and other antibiotics would remain necessary; the proposed advance does not establish a replacement for all antimicrobial care.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability, as defined by this proposal, is dependable translation from an unfamiliar clinical isolate to a treatment that benefits the patient within a useful treatment window. This requires reliable matching or adaptation across varied bacterial isolates and a demonstrated relationship between laboratory susceptibility and clinical response. The supplied material identifies these as the intended challenges, but the retained scientific source does not independently document their extent or continuing openness.

The proposed engineering program must also solve delivery and production together: a preparation must be reproducibly manufactured, reach the relevant infection site and retain useful activity under treatment conditions. Improving the speed of genome engineering or laboratory selection would address only part of that chain. The evidence needed to bridge these stages would include measurements of product consistency, delivery and patient outcomes, rather than laboratory killing alone. These are analytical requirements derived from the platform's intended function.

Bacterial resistance and phage evolution add a further challenge. A platform intended to adapt over time would need to detect loss of susceptibility, determine whether a revised preparation restores useful activity and show that revisions preserve acceptable product properties and clinical performance. Managing an evolving treatment system is a broader problem than demonstrating that one engineered phage has a different bacterial surface specificity. This distinction is part of the proposed research agenda, not an experimentally established solution.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a paper titled “PHEIGES: all-cell-free phage synthesis and selection from engineered genomes,” attributed to Antoine Levrier, Ioannis Karpathakis, Bruce Nash, Steven D. Bowden, Ariel B. Lindner and Vincent Noireaux, with a reported publication date of 12 March 2024 in Nature Communications and DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-46585-1. The research attributes to it cell-free synthesis and selection using engineered T7 genomes, including altered bacterial surface specificity. These are reported findings in the supplied research; the supplied review could not verify them against accessible scientific content.

The access limitation materially affects interpretation. Although the earlier research says its assessment relied on a PubMed abstract after the publisher page failed to open, the artifact available to the supplied review contained only a cookie interstitial. It provided no abstract, methods or results from which to confirm the document's identity or the attributed experiments. Consequently, the reported T7 synthesis, selection and specificity results remain unverified within this record. That limitation does not establish that the reported findings are false.

Even if the attributed PHEIGES experiments are confirmed, their stated scope is a laboratory platform demonstration. They would not by themselves establish reliable treatment of diverse clinical isolates, effective delivery at multiple infection sites or benefit in controlled clinical trials. The supplied record contains no verified quantitative performance results for those outcomes and no basis for describing the general clinical platform as achieved.

The supplied materials also do not establish the field's position as of 1 November 2026. The bounded search record available to the review was empty, and retrieval of the cited page on 11 November 2026 does not demonstrate coverage of developments since the reported 2024 publication. This record therefore cannot determine whether later work has narrowed the remaining gap.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independent centers would prospectively receive previously unseen clinical isolates and use a defined workflow to select or adapt phage preparations across several major pathogens and infection sites. The evaluation should specify the included isolates, selection rules, turnaround requirements and unsuccessful cases in advance. Prospective testing would assess performance beyond familiar examples, while independent execution would test reproducibility. Success would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested scope, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent centers reproducibly match phages to unseen clinical isolates

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: controlled trials would compare the platform's treatment strategy with appropriate standard care, using predefined patient outcomes and a clear account of any accompanying antibiotics or other treatment. Laboratory susceptibility would be evaluated as a predictor of benefit rather than treated as a substitute for it. Pathogens, infection sites, comparators, endpoints and follow-up periods would need explicit operational definitions; the supplied materials do not establish numerical thresholds or consensus standards for them.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled trials demonstrate patient benefit against appropriate standard care

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical demonstration: participating centers would show reproducible manufacturing and reliable delivery within the tested clinical settings, including when preparations are adapted. Follow-up would assess resistance, recurrence and effects on non-target microbes. Results should identify where matching fails, where laboratory activity does not translate into benefit and which settings remain outside the demonstrated capability. These boundaries are part of a convincing platform evaluation.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible manufacturing and reliable delivery with documented clinical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Conceptual relationship to MIC-07, “Programmable, reversible living therapies in the human microbiome”: both concern controllable biological interventions in human-associated microbial systems. MIC-05 centers on phage targeting of bacterial pathogens and adaptation of treatment; MIC-07 centers on programming and reversing living therapeutic functions. MIC-12, “A causal map from microbial metabolites to host phenotypes,” could help interpret indirect host effects, but causal metabolite mapping is distinct from establishing phage treatment efficacy.

Conceptual relationship to MIC-08, “Broadly effective control of bacterial antibiotic persistence,” and MIC-09, “Forecasting horizontal gene transfer and resistance spread in microbial communities”: all concern obstacles to durable antimicrobial success. Antibiotic persistence, bacterial resistance to phages and spread of resistance determinants are different phenomena. Effective phage treatment would not by itself demonstrate control of antibiotic persistence or provide a predictive theory of resistance spread.

Conceptual relationship to MIC-02, “A predictive theory of microbial communities,” and MIC-10, “Programmable microbial consortia for durable ecosystem functions”: community prediction and design could inform assessment of non-target effects or longer-term ecological responses to treatment. MIC-05's defining outcome remains clinical control of an infection. MIC-11, “Quantifying how environmental viruses control biogeochemical fluxes,” shares an interest in virus–microbe interactions but concerns environmental processes rather than patient treatment.

Conceptual relationship to MIC-01, “An autonomously reproducing cell built from defined components,” and MIC-06, “A predictive whole-cell model for microbial design”: these entries share interests in biological construction or prediction. Cell-free phage synthesis, if verified, would be a distinct capability from building an autonomously reproducing cell or predicting whole-cell behavior. Neither of those broader achievements is a stated prerequisite for the treatment platform.

Conceptual relationship to MIC-03, “Routine experimental access to microbial dark matter,” and MIC-04, “Reliable nitrogen-fixing microbial partnerships for major cereal crops”: experimental access and reproducible microbial interactions are shared themes, but the target capabilities differ. Access to previously inaccessible microbes does not establish a clinical treatment workflow, and reliable crop partnerships concern sustained agricultural function rather than pathogen elimination. These comparisons are inferred from the supplied roster titles.

brief.title: Reliable infection treatment with bacteria-killing viruses
possible: If you had a hard-to-treat bacterial infection, doctors could use a repeatable process to match your bacteria to phages—viruses that infect bacteria. They could select or adapt suitable phages, produce a consistent treatment and deliver it to the infection.
why: Clinicians would gain a reusable treatment process for diverse infections, including those that resist antibiotics. Each new patient's bacteria could be matched to a suitable preparation instead of requiring a separate treatment-development effort.
Narrow targeting could also help preserve other microbes while treating the bacteria causing illness.

sources.showed: They made engineered phages without living cells and selected variants with altered bacterial targeting. They also demonstrated a link between the phages' genetic instructions and their resulting traits.
sources.quote: We further demonstrate a significant genotype-phenotype linkage of phage assembly in bulk TXTL.
sources.cited_for: The work supports laboratory engineering, production and selection of phages with altered targeting.
sources.not_established: It does not establish reliable matching across diverse patient bacteria, delivery to infections or patient benefit.

sources.who: Queen Astrid Military Hospital, KU Leuven and Sciensano
sources.showed: A retrospective study examined personalized phage treatment in 100 consecutive cases. It reported clinical improvement and bacterial clearance, often alongside antibiotics, without a control group.
sources.quote: We observed a combination of antibiotic re-sensitization and reduced virulence in bacteriophage-resistant bacterial isolates that emerged during BT.
sources.cited_for: The study supports practical experience with personalized phage treatment and documents bacterial changes during treatment.
sources.not_established: The uncontrolled study cannot establish how much phages contributed to improvement or predict results across patients.

sources.who: Shimin Jasmine Chung, Yang Liu and colleagues
sources.showed: A patient with a persistent infection around a replacement blood vessel received selected phages alongside antibiotics. Scans improved, and the patient remained clinically well.
sources.quote: The patient remains clinically well on follow-up.
sources.cited_for: The case demonstrates an individualized treatment workflow that combined selected phages with antibiotics.
sources.not_established: A single case cannot separate the effects of phages from those of antibiotics and surgery or establish general effectiveness.

shown: Antoine Levrier and colleagues have demonstrated laboratory engineering and selection of phages without living cells. Their system produced engineered phages within a day and selected variants that recognize different bacterial surface structures.

The Belgian consortium has taken personalized phage treatment into hospitals and reported improvement in an uncontrolled patient series. Chung and colleagues also reported improvement in a single patient receiving phages alongside antibiotics. These results do not establish benefit in controlled trials.
missing: Independent centers have yet to demonstrate dependable matching across unfamiliar patient bacteria within a useful treatment window.
Controlled trials must establish patient benefit against appropriate standard care and test whether laboratory killing predicts that benefit.
A general system still needs consistent production, reliable delivery and treatment revisions that preserve quality and clinical performance.

milestones.label: Independent centers reliably match phages to unfamiliar patient bacteria
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would have to prospectively match previously unseen patient bacteria across major pathogens and infection sites, recording timing and failures. This would establish reproducible breadth within the tested scope.

milestones.label: Controlled trials establish patient benefit against standard care
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show patient benefit against appropriate standard care, accounting for accompanying treatments. This would establish whether laboratory matching translates into clinical benefit.

milestones.label: Consistent production and delivery have clear clinical boundaries
milestones.explanation: Centers would have to demonstrate consistent production and delivery after adaptation, tracking resistance, recurrence, effects on other microbes and failures. This would define where treatment remains dependable.

uncertain: How broadly can phages cover different bacteria and infection sites?
How long can revised treatments stay effective as bacteria develop resistance, and how do they affect other microbes?
Which treatment windows, outcome measures and follow-up periods should define success?

page.title: Personalized bacteriophage therapy
page.definition: A treatment system matches bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—to each patient's bacterial isolate, a cultured sample of the infecting strain. It permits selection or adaptation of phages between patients while maintaining product quality and demonstrating clinical benefit within defined indications.

goal.need: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance caused an estimated 1.14 million deaths worldwide in 2021. Treatment matching also limits access: 124 of 260 requests analysed by a Belgian phage programme concerned bacterial species for which its collection contained no phages. Personalized phage therapy addresses the need to connect isolate matching, production and clinical treatment.

figures.caption: Estimated worldwide mortality associated with bacterial antimicrobial resistance in 2021.
figures.note: Attributable deaths compare resistant with susceptible infections; associated deaths compare resistant infection with no infection. These estimates overlap.

statements.context: ESKAPE comprises Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacter species. The call supports preclinical development.

statements.context: The gaps concern practical guidance and specifications for preparing and administering personalized phage therapy.

completion.title: The MHRA licenses phage therapy with patient-specific selection or adaptation of phage composition.
completion.criterion: The MHRA grants a UK marketing authorisation for a phage medicinal product whose authorised use permits patient-specific selection or adaptation of phage composition. The authorisation covers the manufacturing controls and composition changes used by the system and establishes therapeutic efficacy and a positive benefit–risk balance in the stated indication. This test establishes capability within that indication; it specifies no universal pathogen coverage.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas, applying a patient-specific-composition scope to the MHRA marketing-authorisation route.
completion.basis: MHRA guidance defines product-licensing requirements; Horizon Europe includes regularly updated personalized preparations. Searches of MHRA guidance, EMA material, NIH calls and society guidance found no acceptance test for a general adaptable platform, including required pathogen breadth or matching time. Requiring the licence to cover patient-specific composition is an Atlas scope choice, limited to the authorised indication.

milestones.title: Selected or adapted phages show lytic activity against their target bacterial isolate.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate bacterial killing or productive phage infection of the target isolate using susceptibility testing. ARLG identifies no validated clinical susceptibility breakpoint. On 12 March 2024, PHEIGES reported cell-free T7 engineering and selection for altered bacterial-surface recognition, producing up to 10^11 plaque-forming units (PFU)/mL within one day on laboratory Escherichia coli hosts. Chung and colleagues screened four clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates and identified eight infective phages.
milestones.set_by: Antibacterial Resistance Leadership Group Phage Taskforce, clinical-practice considerations, Questions 7 and 12; published expert consensus.
milestones.threshold_quote: a phage product that has been shown to have microbiologic activity against the targeted bacterial pathogen(s)

milestones.title: A personalized phage active ingredient receives certification for use in pharmacy preparations.
milestones.criterion: Pass the Belgian monograph's genomic safety and batch-quality tests and obtain Sciensano certification for use in a pharmacy-compounded preparation. BT100 applied an administered endotoxin limit of 5 EU/kg body mass/hour, where EU means endotoxin units. Its report of 100 patients treated between 1 January 2008 and 30 April 2022 describes more than 40 certified batches, including pre-adapted phages. Certification establishes batch suitability, without establishing clinical efficacy.
milestones.set_by: Sciensano and the Belgian phage consortium, Belgian bacteriophage active pharmaceutical ingredient monograph as implemented in the published BT100 protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: A certificate allowing the bacteriophage API to be used in pharmaceutical (magistral) preparations is provided by Sciensano upon successful completion of this two-tiered procedure.

milestones.title: A patient completes an approved 14-day course of matched intravenous phages.
milestones.criterion: Complete the approved intravenous three-phage course: daily for two days, then twice daily for 12 days, alongside antibiotics. Chung and colleagues administered this regimen to one 36-year-old woman with P. aeruginosa mediastinitis and vascular graft infection, starting on 23 September 2024; no treatment adverse events were observed. BT100 separately reported improvement in 88/114 infections and bacterial eradication in 65/106 evaluable infections among 100 patients, often alongside antibiotics. These uncontrolled observations cannot establish a phage treatment effect.
milestones.set_by: SingHealth Centralized Institutional Review Board, CIRB 2023/2415, and the published compassionate-use protocol; the regimen was specified for one P. aeruginosa graft-infection case.
milestones.threshold_quote: daily on the first 2 days, and twice daily for the remaining 12 days

milestones.title: Matched phages reduce bacterial burden versus placebo at a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
milestones.criterion: Meet CYPHY's primary microbiological efficacy test: a greater reduction in log10 P. aeruginosa sputum colony-forming units/mL from baseline to day 14 with isolate-matched inhaled phages than with placebo, following seven treatment days, at two-sided alpha 0.05. The registry records eight randomized participants, four per arm. In their paper published on 29 April 2025, the investigators state that CYPHY did not meet its prespecified microbiological efficacy endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Yale University, CYPHY protocol 2000029160, version 11 dated 29 November 2022, NCT04684641; this endpoint is specific to P. aeruginosa infection in adults with cystic fibrosis.
milestones.threshold_quote:
the significance will be
established at the two-sided alpha level of 0.05.

milestones.title: A multicentre, multinational randomized trial demonstrates phage therapy's safety and efficacy.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate safety and efficacy in a multicentre, multinational randomized controlled trial of personalized phage therapy for difficult-to-treat bacterial infection, alone or with standard care. Horizon Europe explicitly includes regularly updated personalized preparations. The programme sets no common sample size, effect-size cutoff or statistical threshold; these require an indication-specific protocol.
milestones.set_by: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme 2025, Health, HORIZON-HLTH-2025-01-DISEASE-01, pages 43–44; the call covers personalized preparations and fixed cocktails.
milestones.threshold_quote:
multicenter, multinational randomised controlled clinical trial (RCT) to generate scientific
evidence demonstrating safety and efficacy of phage-based therapy

not_found: No published platform-wide threshold for pathogen coverage, matching turnaround or reproducibility between centres was found.
No UK marketing authorisation explicitly covering patient-specific phage replacement was located.
No published result from a multicentre, multinational randomized trial of regularly updated personalized phage therapy was located.
The full recommendation tables of the 2026 society guideline and the AWMF registry text could not be retrieved; its abstract was accessible.
ClinicalTrials.gov's CYPHY results page did not render readable results text; its indexed record supplies enrolment, and the investigators' paper supplies the efficacy outcome.

results.detail: The hosts were three laboratory mutant strains; the paper does not report testing patient isolates.
results.quote: Unlike T7 WT, all mutants exhibited a broad infection spectrum.
